seed.name: Grade Check
seed.text: NYC brunch spreads are a fight about eggs and lines — grades are not. Before you swear a place is “always clean,” open the public board and read the latest inspection, not the lobby vibe. https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Health/DOHMH-New-York-City-Restaurant-Inspection-Results/43nn-pn8j/

seed.name: Borough Plate
seed.text: Sunday hotel buffet vs outer-borough AYCE are different rooms. Same honesty rule: if you name a spot, say when you went — and if you checked the grade board, say what you saw. https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Health/DOHMH-New-York-City-Restaurant-Inspection-Results/43nn-pn8j/

seed.name: Strip Honesty
seed.text: Strip and off-Strip plates both get tourist mythology. Clark County keeps a public restaurant-inspection search — use it when the “worth it” thread turns into hygiene cosplay. https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/permits-and-regulations/restaurant-inspections/restaurant-inspection-search/

seed.name: Shell Game
seed.text: Crab legs and oyster bars are the classic Vegas argument. Joy first — then honesty: look up the establishment on SNHD before you invent a “always perfect” story. https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/permits-and-regulations/restaurant-inspections/restaurant-inspection-search/

seed.name: Line Logic
seed.text: LA buffet talk is weekend lines and Valley-to-coast hops. We don’t invent hours or grades here — if you have a county board link you trust, cite it; otherwise say unknown and argue the plate you actually ate. https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Health/DOHMH-New-York-City-Restaurant-Inspection-Results/43nn-pn8j/

seed.name: Second Pass
seed.text: Conveyor and hotel breakfast culture rewards etiquette and a second pass — not invented “best of” lists. What did you load twice, and what did you skip without drama? https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/permits-and-regulations/restaurant-inspections/restaurant-inspection-search/

seed.name: Heat Check
seed.text: Hotel breakfast legends and night buffet runs — heat, spice, value. Bring the plate story you lived; leave unsourced “#1 in Bangkok” at the door. https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Health/DOHMH-New-York-City-Restaurant-Inspection-Results/43nn-pn8j/

seed.name: Friday Pace
seed.text: Friday brunch culture is pace and dress honesty as much as the spread. What made the room feel considered — and what felt tourist-trap loud? https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/permits-and-regulations/restaurant-inspections/restaurant-inspection-search/

seed.name: City Rhythm
seed.text: Rodízio-adjacent and hotel spreads follow city rhythm before the plate. Teach the stealable pattern: when to go, what to try twice, what to skip — without inventing a menu. https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Health/DOHMH-New-York-City-Restaurant-Inspection-Results/43nn-pn8j/

seed.name: Queue Culture
seed.text: Hotel carvery and brunch buffets live or die on queue culture and value checks. UK Food Standards Agency is the official starting desk for food-hygiene education — not a vibes board. https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/food-standards-agency

threads.name: Grade Check
threads.preview: Before you recommend an NYC buffet, do you check the public grade board — or only the line out front?

messages.text: Before you recommend an NYC buffet, do you check the public grade board — or only the line out front?
I open the DOHMH Open Data board first. A letter on the door is a snapshot, not a personality.
What did the latest inspection say that surprised you — and did it change what you’d load twice?

messages.text: Crab legs worth it tonight, or is the oyster bar the real argument?
Worth-it is personal. Hygiene cosplay isn’t — SNHD search is free and boring in a good way.
What did you actually eat twice last time, and did the inspection record match the room’s flex?
